name: pdk-dbt-unirate-dbt
instr:
We stopped calling the API from the warehouse. Our treasury team's daily rates file now goes in with dbt seed as unirate__exchange_rates, as the README describes. Most models use the macros' default relation, some pass the file as rates_relation. Samples of the file and of our orders export are in /data/treasury and /data/shop.

Our orders come in many currencies and we report in USD, EUR and GBP, but most amounts from unirate.convert_currency come back NULL. dbt build also fails once the file is seeded, and models that pass date_column without rates_relation don't compile. We don't have the Pro history model, so dated lookups should read the seeded file too.

unirate.get_rate, unirate.get_historical_rate and unirate.convert_currency should give the rate between any two currencies the file links through its quotes, whatever its base currency is. Each pair of currencies counts at its latest quote, or, when date_column is given, its latest quote on or before that date. A currency argument can be a code as today ('GBP', 'usd') or a qualified column like 'o.currency', which is read per row. When both currencies of a row are the same, convert_currency returns the amount unchanged.

A result should be NULL only when a quote it needs has no rate on or before the date. None of the sample orders should come out NULL in USD, EUR or GBP. dbt build has to pass with the file seeded, as do the existing integration tests in /app/integration_tests.
